Theme

Travel & transport

hotel noun

also inn, double room, single room, hole in the wall, cheap lodgings, stay at a hotel

classical

Traupman 174
the Libellus I gloss, after Traupman 174: dēversōrium -ī n: domus in quā viātōrēs mercēde pernoctant, “a house where travellers stay the night for payment”
Traupman 329

dēversōrium, dēversōriī n.

noun, second declension

mercēde — for payment.

Other words

  • hospitium, hospitiī n.

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 174

  • stabulum, stabulī n. — cheap lodging, tavern, a hole in the wall

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 328

    A humble dwelling, and a low inn or tavern (Petronius, the Digest; Lewis & Short); also a stable.

Examples

  • conclāve duōrum lectōrum

    a double roomTraupman 306

  • cubiculum ūnīus lectī

    a single roomTraupman 379

  • in dēversōriō morārī

    to stay at a hotelTraupman 329

See also check in, check out, floor, spend the night.
